name: Cisco IOS — Login Brute Force Against Device
description: Fires when a single Cisco IOS device logs 30 or more 'Login failed' syslog messages within an hour — the management-interface brute-force signature, against a baseline of roughly 2-3 failures/day. Attackers guess VTY/console/enable credentials to gain device control and pivot or alter routing. Implemented as a Threshold rule grouped by device hostname. Maps to ATT&CK Credential Access T1110 (Brute Force).
note:
### Investigation
1. Confirm the failure burst is concentrated on one device (log.syslog.hostname) and exceeds its normal ~2-3/day baseline.
2. Identify the source (log.source.address or the address embedded in message) — a known NMS/backup poller or an unexpected host?
3. Check for a subsequent successful login from the same source after the failures (compromise).
4. Correlate other devices hit by the same source (estate-wide credential attack).
5. Escalate on success-after-failures or an unrecognized source targeting management planes.

### False positives / benign
Monitoring/NMS churn and a mis-scheduled backup or poller with stale credentials can produce sustained 'Login failed' bursts from a fixed, known source. Distinguish by whether log.source.address is an inventoried management system (known_infrastructure) and whether a success ever follows — legitimate pollers fail consistently without succeeding interactively, whereas an attack often ends in a success or rotates usernames. Fix the stale-credential source rather than allowlisting the device.

### Notes
BLOCKED_BY_TELEMETRY: Cisco IOS @timestamp is future-dated; the rule cannot fire until the ingestion clock is fixed.
